description: See, hear, and interact on your local devices.

summary.one_liner: MiniCPM-V and MiniCPM-o are open multimodal model families (vision-language and 9B omnimodal) from THUNLP and ModelBest, aimed at running on local and mobile devices.
summary.what_it_does: The README introduces MiniCPM-V 4.7 (35B-A3B MoE and 1B variants) for image, multi-image, document and video understanding, and MiniCPM-o 4.5, a 9B end-to-end omnimodal model that takes continuous video and audio input while generating speech and text. It describes Lookahead Expert Scheduling for running the MoE model on-device, with a reported 13+ tokens/s on an iPhone 17 Pro Max. Model weights are published in BF16, FP8, int4, AWQ, GPTQ and GGUF formats, plus DSpark speculative decoding heads. The README also lists MiniCPM-OCR models, a Self-Replay Fine-Tuning (SRFT) method, fine-tuning, live demo, local deployment, cookbook and API access. Model weights are on Hugging Face, with vLLM and Ollama mentioned as supported options.
use_cases: run a multimodal vision-language model on a phone or laptop
document and OCR text extraction from images and PDFs
real-time voice and video conversation with an AI model
voice cloning and role-play from a reference audio clip
fine-tune a multimodal model on custom data
serve a vision-language model with vLLM or Ollama
how_to_run: Download model weights from Hugging Face (see the Model weights section for MiniCPM-V 4.7 or MiniCPM-o 4.5)
Follow the Local deployment guide linked from the Get started section
Use the vLLM option listed under Model weights for serving
Or run the model through Ollama, which the README says carries MiniCPM-V 4.6
notable: MiniCPM-o 4.5 is a 9B model that can see, hear and speak at the same time in full-duplex mode
MiniCPM-V 4.7 35B-A3B is described as the first open-source MoE model to run smoothly on-device
Lookahead Expert Scheduling loads MoE experts from SSD with overlapping computation, reported as a 5x speedup on real devices
Supports iOS, Android, HarmonyOS and several chip platforms including Intel, AMD, Arm, Rockchip and Houmo
Released as weights in many formats, including GGUF for CPU inference
caveats: The README does not give full setup steps in the text; deployment details are in linked guides
Quantization notes say some variants use different methods (bitsandbytes for 1B int4, W4A16 for AWQ and GPTQ)
The 35B-A3B model is large, and the on-device speed figure is reported for one iPhone model only
